$Comment: Tools, paid out by Trim Work. A sawyer wears a hatchet down, so the yard keeps them in
gear: a spare hatchet now and then, repair kits more often than that, and a small sapling and
light bonus for a well-invested luck tree.
THE TWO TOOL ROLLS READ WOODCUTTING LEVEL ALONE, deliberately, matching the paradigm this pack
follows everywhere: level picks the floor, so a hatchet or a repair kit tracks where the worker
is in their trade rather than how lucky the run was. The third roll below is the one place in
this file that reads luck, on its own ladder with its own floors.
EACH TOOL ROLL PAIRS A CHANCE WITH A LADDER, which is what keeps the two of them to two rolls
rather than six. The Chance decides whether anything is handed over at all; the Ladder then
decides WHICH tier, and because floors are highest-wins and not cumulative, exactly one item
comes out of each roll. A worker at level ninety gets the top tier and nothing else, never one
of each.
EVERY LADDER STARTS AT ZERO on purpose, below the level the quest that opens Trim Work asks for.
A ladder grants NOTHING when every floor sits above the worker's reading, so the bottom rung is
what keeps a roll that fired from handing over an empty hand if a level ever comes in lower than
the quest's gate implies. Keep it when you re-tune the rungs above it.
THE HATCHET LADDER'S TOP FLOOR IS A REPAIR KIT, not a hatchet, and that is deliberate: the
questline Trim Work sits beside ends in a hatchet carrying stats no vanilla tool has, so anybody
standing at this floor already carries something better than anything this table could hand
over. A spare Copper, Iron or Thorium hatchet below that floor is still a genuine upgrade for
whoever has not reached the questline's own reward yet.
Repair kits come on roughly one run in eight, against a hatchet at about one run in twenty,
because a kit is upkeep and a hatchet is a small event. Only the hatchet roll carries a Cue: a
repair kit lands too often to make each one feel special, and a chime for it would cheapen the
ones that matter.
Name: Mmo_Sawmill_Trim_Supply

Rolls.$Comment: A spare hatchet, at the tier the worker's level has earned.

A repair kit instead of a hatchet: anybody reading this high already carries a hatchet no spare here could match.

Rolls.$Comment: Repair kits, the everyday upkeep, at the tier the worker's level has earned.

Floors.$Comment: The crude kit covers everything below the iron rung, starting at zero so the roll always has a floor to land on.

Rolls.$Comment: A small bonus for a well-invested luck tree: extra saplings, and a lantern once that investment is heavy. Reads MMO_Luck_WOODCUTTING alone, on its own floors, with no Chance gating it - it always resolves, and its zero floor pays a token sapling rather than nothing.
